questions.q: What does the article give as the only practical solution to grievances against others?
options: To make them public
Not quite. The article says: To forget them, of one’s own accord, rather than investigate or dwell on them.
To keep a careful record of them
Not quite. The article says: To forget them, of one’s own accord, rather than investigate or dwell on them.
To prove each complaint true or false
Not quite. The article says: To forget them, of one’s own accord, rather than investigate or dwell on them.
To forget them, of one’s own accord, rather than investigate or dwell on them
Yes. Looking into them usually makes things worse.
questions.rationale: “The only practical thing that you can do in this regard is to not store in your mind any complaints you might have against others.”

questions.q: When making peace, each side fears the other may not keep its word. What does the Quran (8:61-62) advise?
options: Add harder conditions to the treaty
Not quite. The article says: Make peace all the same and put your trust in God.
Make peace all the same and put your trust in God
Right. Suspicion is the great obstacle to peace.
Make peace only with the weak
Not quite. The article says: Make peace all the same and put your trust in God.
Wait for firm guarantees first
Not quite. The article says: Make peace all the same and put your trust in God.
questions.rationale: “Then if they should be inclined to make peace, make peace with them, and put your trust in God… Should they seek to deceive you, God is enough for you.”

questions.q: Why does the article advise against pressing controversial points during a settlement?
options: Because written terms settle everything
Not quite. The article says: It stirs the other side’s ego and makes agreement harder; avoiding controversy reveals common ground.
Because the other side will forget them
Not quite. The article says: It stirs the other side’s ego and makes agreement harder; avoiding controversy reveals common ground.
Because such points are never important
Not quite. The article says: It stirs the other side’s ego and makes agreement harder; avoiding controversy reveals common ground.
It stirs the other side’s ego and makes agreement harder; avoiding controversy reveals common ground
Well reasoned. Peace needs a unilateral first step.
questions.rationale: “If you insist on raising controversial points, you will arouse the ego of the other party and the desired settlement will become more difficult to achieve than ever before.”

questions.q: An old argument against God’s existence was that He cannot be seen. What, according to the article, weakened it?
options: Science itself found that much of nature – such as subatomic particles – exists though unobservable
Yes. Unseen does not mean unreal.
Philosophers stopped discussing it
Not quite. The article says: Science itself found that much of nature – such as subatomic particles – exists though unobservable.
Larger telescopes showed the edge of space
Not quite. The article says: Science itself found that much of nature – such as subatomic particles – exists though unobservable.
Ancient records were rediscovered
Not quite. The article says: Science itself found that much of nature – such as subatomic particles – exists though unobservable.
questions.rationale: “It became apparent and accepted that there are many aspects of nature that are invisible yet they exist.”

questions.q: “Which of your Lord’s wonders would you deny?” What does the article say “deny” means here?
options: To destroy them
Not quite. The article says: To ignore them – taking them for granted without acknowledgement.
To argue against them publicly
Not quite. The article says: To ignore them – taking them for granted without acknowledgement.
To forget their names
Not quite. The article says: To ignore them – taking them for granted without acknowledgement.
To ignore them – taking them for granted without acknowledgement
Correct. Reason was given to man to notice and be grateful.
questions.rationale: “By ‘deny’ is meant to ignore or to not acknowledge… We simply take them for granted.”

questions.q: What method of learning English did Lenin describe as “the most rational”?
options: Memorising a dictionary
Not quite. The article says: Translating a book into his own language and then back into English without looking at the original.
Reading newspapers aloud
Not quite. The article says: Translating a book into his own language and then back into English without looking at the original.
Translating a book into his own language and then back into English without looking at the original
Right. Later he also listened closely to speakers wherever he could.
Writing letters to English friends
Not quite. The article says: Translating a book into his own language and then back into English without looking at the original.
questions.rationale: “Not only did they translate the book from English into their native Russian, but Lenin also used to translate it back into English, without referring to the original text.”

questions.q: What general way to success does the article take from this example?
options: Wait for a good teacher to appear
Not quite. The article says: Take up the best example of those before you and build on it with sustained hard work of your own.
Take up the best example of those before you and build on it with sustained hard work of your own
Well read. It may take years, but it works.
Change methods frequently
Not quite. The article says: Take up the best example of those before you and build on it with sustained hard work of your own.
Rely on natural talent
Not quite. The article says: Take up the best example of those before you and build on it with sustained hard work of your own.
questions.rationale: “While taking up the best traditions of the past, we are to build upon them for the future with sheer hard work of our own.”

questions.q: What does the rose plant symbolise in the article?
options: Flowers and thorns sharing one stem without clashing – as different people should live together in society
Yes. A lesson from nature in peaceful living.
The reward of careful gardening
Not quite. The article says: Flowers and thorns sharing one stem without clashing – as different people should live together in society.
The danger hidden in pleasant things
Not quite. The article says: Flowers and thorns sharing one stem without clashing – as different people should live together in society.
Beauty that fades quickly
Not quite. The article says: Flowers and thorns sharing one stem without clashing – as different people should live together in society.
questions.rationale: “Both flowers and thorns live together on the stem of a rose plant, but there is no clash between the two… symbolic of how we should live in society.”

questions.q: What price, according to the article, do high positions exact from those who hold them?
options: Their friendships
Not quite. The article says: Their freedom – mental, moral, emotional and physical.
Their health
Not quite. The article says: Their freedom – mental, moral, emotional and physical.
Their wealth
Not quite. The article says: Their freedom – mental, moral, emotional and physical.
Their freedom – mental, moral, emotional and physical
Exactly. One who resigned felt “as free as a bird.”
questions.rationale: “The price we pay for them is our freedom—mental, moral, emotional and physical—and surely renunciation of such freedom is too great a price to pay.”

questions.q: For a single need of man to be met, countless factors in nature must work together. What does the commentary conclude from this?
options: Human needs are met by chance
Not quite. The article says: Only the One who controls the whole universe could arrange it – so He alone deserves worship.
Only the One who controls the whole universe could arrange it – so He alone deserves worship
Well reasoned. Coordination points to one Lord.
Each factor has its own separate ruler
Not quite. The article says: Only the One who controls the whole universe could arrange it – so He alone deserves worship.
Nature is too complicated to understand
Not quite. The article says: Only the One who controls the whole universe could arrange it – so He alone deserves worship.
questions.rationale: “To cause a single event to take place, it is necessary to activate innumerable factors, and this can be done only by that Being who has control of the whole universe.”
